findings.failure_path: Delete at least one line from an owner Markdown file and chmod another owner Markdown file from 100644 to 100755. Both paths appear as M under --name-status; the chmod contributes 0/0 to --numstat while the deletion keeps total additions at zero and deletions positive. The owner therefore passes source-refuted even though its mode changed without RED evidence.
findings.smallest_fix: Inspect old and new tree modes for every eligible path, require both entries to be regular blobs with identical modes, and add a chmod-plus-deletion regression case.

findings.failure_path: Run the new test normally against the candidate. Compliant case A returns zero, but EXPECT_A_GREEN defaults to 0, so the script records a failure and exits nonzero even though the feature works.
findings.smallest_fix: Default the candidate test to EXPECT_A_GREEN=1 and set EXPECT_A_GREEN=0 explicitly only in the separate pre-change RED-baseline invocation.

findings.failure_path: A source-refuted withdrawal that adds only non-normative explanatory prose is rejected by the zero-added-lines classifier, but the emitted fix text says only that no normative rule line may be added. Following that diagnostic leaves the gate failing with no explanation of the actual Markdown-only, M-status, zero-addition requirement.
findings.smallest_fix: Rewrite the diagnostic to state the exact structural predicate: modified regular Markdown paths only, unchanged modes, zero added lines, and at least one deleted line.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Failed: the pure-deletion classifier treats name-status M as proof of an ordinary content-only modification, allowing an unvouched Markdown mode change to accompany a deletion.
The shared gate can falsely approve an owner package that deletes prose while making another Markdown file executable, weakening the evidence boundary.
A pure Markdown deletion plus chmod on another owner Markdown file yields M statuses, zero added lines, and positive deletions, so source-refuted passes without accounting for the mode mutation.
The cases omit mode-change coverage, and the new test defaults to expecting compliant case A to remain red, so a normal invocation fails against the implemented behavior.
Status parsing is additive, but the classifier and CLI diagnostic no longer consistently implement the documented pure-deletion contract.
No irreversible migration is present, but the shared gate is not release-ready until the false-green mode path and false-red test entrypoint are corrected.
The failure diagnostic still describes a normative-line heuristic instead of the implemented zero-addition, Markdown-only structural constraint, directing operators toward an ineffective repair.
Containment is incomplete because Git status M does not establish unchanged mode or regular-file identity, despite those being required properties of the source-refuted exemption.
